observation.visible_scene: Open flames burning against a uniform, featureless black background. The fire is anchored along the bottom edge and fills the center and right portions of the frame, while the left side stays dark throughout. The flame body shows a bright yellow-white base near the bottom that fades to orange and red toward the tips.
visible_changes: The flame shape continuously deforms frame to frame: tongues stretch upward, curl into hooks, thin into wisps, and broaden into rounded lobes (e.g., the curled tongue at left in frame 12, the tall narrow column in frame 17).
The overall height of the flame mass oscillates: it drops low and compact in frames 3-4 and 21-23, then grows tall and reaches near the top edge in frames 2, 6, 14, 24-25, 32-33, 36.

The horizontal position of the main flame body shifts modestly but stays right-of-center: it leans toward the right edge in frames 3-4, 19-23, 30, 34, 37-40 and re-centers in frames 1, 6-8, 12-17, 31-33, 41.

Small detached flame fragments appear above the main body at various moments (top-left tongue in frame 1, a wisp at top-center in frames 9, 18, 22, 28, 37), behaving as separate rising tongues rather than occluded parts of one column.
The bright core at the bottom persists across all frames, indicating the flame source region remains in roughly the same place while the upper structure flickers.
No single smooth start or stop is visible; the motion is already ongoing at t=0 and still ongoing at t=3.333.
outside_clip_unknowns: The fuel or object feeding the fire is not visible (frame edges crop the base).
What happens before t=0 and after t=3.333 is unknown; the excerpt is a temporal crop, so the fire does not necessarily begin or end here.
Airflow, wind, or any cause of the flickering is not observable.
uncertain_details: Camera motion cannot be confirmed or ruled out because the background is pure black with no reference points; the apparent left-right drift of the flame is treated as object movement, but a slight camera pan cannot be excluded.
Whether the small top wisps are physically separate flame pockets or motion-blur of a single tongue is ambiguous at this frame rate.
The exact brightness changes may partly reflect sensor/exposure flicker rather than pure flame behavior.
